title: The roles of Model Spec and Constitution

opening.headline: Why does the model reject some requests and comply with others? Those standards are not in the Usage Policy but in other documents.
body: In the same app, the same model will follow some instructions and reject others. No amount of reading of the Acceptable Use Policy can explain this difference because the Acceptable Use Policy is a document that sets out the obligations of people and organizations. How the model is intended to behave is contained in a separate document.

In this class, OpenAI's Model Specification and Anthropic's Constitution are read side by side. After looking at how the two documents organize conflict of instructions and how they are different from the usage policy, we will explain the basis for selecting the model in cases where instructions conflict. At the end, we outline where company policies meet model behavior.
opening.objectivesLead: By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:
objectives: Can explain the role and structure of Model Specification and Constitution
Distinguish between the roles of policy documents and action principles documents.

screens.title: Why does the same model reject some and follow others?
screens.lead:
Read the three situations in the counseling app and first predict how the model will behave in each.

Policy base date: 2026-10-23. Distinguish between the version currently in effect and the version scheduled to be implemented. Anthropic has released the 2026-11-12 enforcement version, so you should check again for changes in the enforcement date and high-risk areas and disclosure obligations before actual operation.

visual.alt: An illustration listing three situations where system instructions and user requests conflict in a counseling app as cards.
labels: System instruction: Do not talk about the weather / User: Ask about the weather
Operator Instructions: Tell User False Information
User request to answer in a different format than previous instructions

paragraphs: Let's say a company running a counseling app writes "Don't talk about the weather" in its system instructions. But the user asks about the weather. Will the model follow these instructions? In the second situation, the operator is instructed to “tell the user false information.” In the third situation, the user is asked to answer in a format different from the previously established format.

The model sometimes follows instructions and sometimes refuses. However, this standard is not written in the usage policy. A usage policy is a document that sets out how people and organizations should use a model, and violations result in enforcement such as warnings or usage restrictions. It does not address what the model itself takes precedence between instructions.

The standards are contained in a document that discloses the model behavioral principles. OpenAI releases Model Spec, and Anthropic releases Claude's Constitution. This lesson focuses on understanding what these two documents are and how they differ from their usage policies.

callout.label: Things to think about
callout.text: Which of the three situations would the model be more likely to follow and which would it be more likely to reject? Check with evidence in the explanation at the end of class.

screens.outro: First, let's recall your experience with behavioral principles documents.

screens.title: Have you ever read the Principles of Conduct document?
screens.lead: When you select a question, the instructor's thoughts unfold. The answer will not be submitted, so think of it yourself first and then check.

items.prompt: Have you ever read a document explaining why a model declined?
items.answer: Most people just read the rejection message and move on. However, both companies provide public documentation of the intended behavior of their models. Knowing this document will help you ensure that the rejection was not a coincidence and came from written principles.

items.prompt: Were you thinking that the principles followed by the usage policy and the model were the same document?
items.answer: It's a common misconception. The usage policy addresses the obligations of users and the organization and is subject to enforcement for violations. Behavioral principles documents address how the model should behave and serve as a basis for training and evaluation. This difference is the axis of the entire class.

items.prompt: When system prompts and user requests conflict, which side do you expect to win?
items.answer: I think usually the one who speaks later, or is more specific, wins. In practice, the level of authority is determined by the source of the instructions. Let's look at the next screen to see how the two documents resolve this conflict.

screens.outro: Now, let’s open OpenAI’s Model Specification structure.

screens.title: Structure of Model Spec: Ladder of authority levels
screens.lead: Model Spec resolves conflicts by assigning a level of authority to each instruction. Select the right arrow to go up the ladder one step at a time and check the meaning of each step.

visual.alt: A diagram showing the level of authority from root to guideline in the shape of a ladder.
labels: Root cannot be changed even with system messages

steps.title: Structure of the document
steps.body: The Model Spec is structured in the following order: overview, definitions, chain of commands corresponding to the hierarchy of instructions, staying in scope, finding the truth together, doing what's best, style, and under-18 principles. Each section of the document displays permission levels, so you can see at a glance which rules are fixed and which can be adjusted.

steps.title: Root and System
steps.body: Root is a fundamental rule that cannot be changed by system messages, developers, or users. Most are prohibitive rules that avoid fatal danger, physical harm, or breaking the law. The System below is the rules set by OpenAI, and can be changed with system messages, but not by developers or users.

steps.title: Developer and User
steps.body: Developer is the stage of a developer giving instructions through API. The model follows developer instructions unless blocked by root or system instructions. User is the end-user level, which honors user requests as long as they do not conflict with developer or system instructions. When the two are together, the power of developer direction is higher.

steps.title: Guideline
steps.body: Guidelines are default values that can be changed implicitly, like context clues. Unlike User stage defaults, which can only be changed explicitly, they are more flexible. The documentation explains that as much instruction as possible is placed at this stage to avoid overly intruding the user.

steps.title: Conflict Resolution Rules
steps.body: High-authority instructions trump low-privilege instructions, and later messages can replace earlier instructions at the same stage. Untrusted data, such as text in quotes or tool output, is by default unprivileged and treated as information only. While these rules give developers and users freedom to adjust, they also set limits.

screens.outro: If the Model Spec organizes instructions into levels of authority, what is the structure of the Constitution?

screens.title: Structure of the Constitution: Priorities and Subjects
screens.lead: Select each tab to explore the two axes on which Claude's Constitution organizes its actions. The final tab checks how operator instructions are treated.

tabs.label: priority
tabs.body: The Constitution sets out, in order of priority, four properties that a model must adhere to: Firstly, comprehensive safety, secondly, comprehensive ethics, thirdly, compliance with Anthropic guidelines, and fourthly, genuine helpfulness. In cases of conflict, the preceding attribute usually takes precedence, but the document explains that this precedence is comprehensive rather than strict. We also state that in most everyday tasks these properties do not conflict.

tabs.label: subject
tabs.body: The subject is called the principal, and refers to the person on whose behalf the model gives weight to instructions and acts on its behalf. There are three types: Anthropic, operator, and user. An operator is a company or individual who creates a product using an API, and a user is a person who interacts with that product. Different entities have different levels of trust and users do not always take precedence.

tabs.label: operator instructions
tabs.body: The operator is likened to a business owner who dispatches an employee. It is relatively trustworthy, but not unconditional, and if there appears to be a legitimate business reason, it will be followed even if the reason is not stated. The greater the potential for harm, the more context is needed, and some instructions are not followed even if there is good reason to do so. The example of an airline app banning weather stories illustrates this principle.

tabs.label: absolutely prohibited
tabs.body: The Constitution has a hard constraint on not doing anything no matter what you tell it to do. This includes, for example, providing no practical assistance in bioweapon attacks. This line cannot be untied by the operator or user instructions. The model should also inform the user if there is something it cannot help with in the current operator environment, even if it cannot state why.

screens.outro: Now that we have seen the structure of both documents, let's compare their usage policies to sort out the differences in their roles.

screens.title: What is the difference between policy and principle?
screens.lead: Click the toggle to read the same request alternately from the perspective of the Acceptable Use Policy and the Principles of Conduct document. You can compare how the questions answered by the two documents differ.

states.label: Usage Policy
states.body: Usage policies dictate how people and organizations should use the model. So, it answers the question, “Can I use it for this purpose?” Violations result in enforcement actions such as warnings, usage restrictions, and suspensions, and the targets of enforcement are users and organizations with accounts. Usage policies do not dictate how a model responds to a request, but rather outline the responsibilities of the sender of the request. For example, if an in-house representative uses a model for purposes that violate policy, it is the users and the organization that are in trouble. Therefore, when creating company regulations, the usage policy is used as a basis for setting the boundaries of permitted business uses.

states.label: Model Spec and Constitution
states.body: Both documents specify how the model should behave. Therefore, it answers the question “How should the model respond to this request?” and serves as the basis for learning and evaluation. OpenAI states that the Model Specification is a document that describes the model, and the overall product is complemented by other layers, such as the usage policy. Additionally, the Model Spec is not an assertion that the model already behaves perfectly that way, but rather a goal. Model Spec sets the basic behavior, and developers and users adjust it within the acceptable range. This is why, even for the same request, the model's response can vary depending on whether there is a developer instruction or what the user specifies. This is the document to refer to when transferring company regulations to model settings.

screens.outro: Now that you understand the differences in roles, let's unpack how the two documents are used in cases where instructions conflict.

screens.title: Commentary: On what basis does a model make a choice when instructions conflict?
screens.lead: The instructor explains step-by-step the examples of counseling apps that we have seen for the first time. Select the next arrow to proceed.

steps.title: Organize the case
steps.body: The counseling app's system instruction is "Don't talk about the weather," and the user asks about the weather. The model must choose between two instructions. The common starting point of both documents is to first determine where the instructions come from and whether there will be harm if followed.

steps.title: Model Spec Perspective
steps.body: Developer level instructions have higher privileges than User level requests. Not telling the weather is a harmless limitation, so the model follows the developer's instructions. This judgment requires no interpretation and is based on the order of the authority levels.

steps.title: Constitution perspective
steps.body: Telling airline apps not to tell you the weather seems like a legitimate business reason to avoid looking like authoritative advice on flight delays. So the model follows even if there is no reason to do so, and tells the user that it cannot help with this topic. This is to enable users to seek help elsewhere.

steps.title: more dangerous instructions
steps.body: The situation is different if the operator instructs the user to tell false information. These instructions are filtered out by higher-level rules in the Model Spec and by ethical priorities in the Constitution. The greater the likelihood of harm, the more evidence the model requires, and some instructions are not followed even if there are reasons to do so.

steps.title: Summary of results
steps.body: The choice of a model follows three rationales: origin of instructions, potential for harm, and user protection. We follow low-harm restrictions, such as weather bans, and do not follow high-harm requests, such as directives to deceive users. Therefore, the answers to the first three situations become clear.

marks.span: You can narrow down the default behavior of your model by moving it to system instructions
marks.note: In the Model Specification, instructions from the Developer stage have high authority, and in the Constitution, the operator follows them even if there is no legitimate business reason. On this basis, regulations can be incorporated into system instructions to narrow down the default behavior.

marks.span: The root or hard constraint level ban cannot be lifted by regulation.
marks.note: Root rules cannot be changed by system messages or developer instructions, and hard constraints cannot be resolved by any instructions. Even if company regulations try to relax this, the model does not follow.

marks.span: Complemented by operational procedures such as human reviews and logs
marks.note: If you try to solve regulations that are difficult for the model to follow just by setting them, gaps will arise. Given that the document is a stated goal, it should be supplemented with human review and documentation.

marks.span: Reference to determine whether the behavior expected by the regulations is possible
marks.note: Before writing a rule, look in both documents to see if the behavior is default, adjustable, or hard-prohibited to help you create a realistic rule.

screens.outro: Now that I have finished explaining the case, I will summarize the main points of the lesson.

screens.title: Key Takeaway: Policies are user obligations, principles are model behavior.
screens.lead: We organize the contents so far into three categories. Read the paragraphs in turn and think about how they apply to your company's policies.

paragraphs: The Usage Policy addresses the obligations of users and the organization, while the Model Specification and Constitution address the behavior of the model. By distinguishing between the two, you can find different questions in each document: "Can I use it?" and "How does the model react?" OpenAI explains that the Model Specification is a document that describes the model, and the product as a whole is complemented by other layers, such as usage policies.

The two action documents differ in the way they organize their instructions. Model Spec resolves conflict of instructions through the authority levels of Root, System, Developer, User, and Guideline. The Constitution is broken down into the priorities of the four attributes of safety, ethics, compliance with guidelines, and helpfulness, and the division of subjects into Anthropic, Operator, and User. The model follows system dictates without reason, but demands more evidence as harm increases.

Company regulations can be used as follows: Although it is possible to narrow down a model's default behavior with regulations, root-level prohibitions or hard constraints cannot be resolved. Additionally, since both documents are goals that reveal intended actions, differences from actual actions must be checked separately and operating procedures need to be supplemented.

When leaving the rules up to the model, check three things in order: First, look in the documentation to see if this behavior is default or disabled. Second, if it is the default, narrow or adjust it to system instructions. Third, areas that cannot be guaranteed through settings alone are supplemented with human review and logs. By following this order, you will avoid mistakes such as creating regulations that the model will not follow or relying on the settings and omitting operational procedures.

callout.label: Points to remember
callout.text: Actions written down are intentions and goals. You will have to check separately whether they actually behave that way.

checks.intro: Check for yourself how you treat operator instructions. This confirmation is not logged.
checks.q: Which of the following is an appropriate way for Claude's Constitution to treat operator instructions?
options: Refuse all orders without a reason given.
Since it is the employer's instructions, they are followed regardless of whether it is harmful or not.
If there appears to be a legitimate business reason, follow it even if there is no reason, but the greater the harm, the more context is required.
The user's request always takes precedence over the operator's instructions.
checks.explain: The operator is relatively trusting, like the employer sending the employee, but not unconditionally, so the greater the likelihood of harm, the more evidence is needed.

wrong.0: If there appears to be a good reason, it will be followed even if the reason is not stated.
wrong.1: There are cases where instructions that are very harmful may not be followed even if there is a reason.
wrong.3: Different subjects have different levels of trust and users do not always take precedence.

checks.correctFeedback: That's right. We pointed out both aspects: follow it even if there is no reason, but require more evidence as the harm increases.
checks.incorrectFeedback: The explanation you chose is biased towards one extreme. Think back to the expatriate analogy.

checks.intro: Match the roles of the documents identified earlier. For each term on the left, choose an appropriate explanation from the right.
checks.q: Match the following terms and descriptions
right: A model action document that organizes instructional conflicts into authority levels.
People and organizations decide how to use it and enforcement follows if it is violated.
An absolute no-no line, no matter what instructions you give.
A document that organizes actions by prioritizing attributes such as safety and ethics and classifying subjects.
checks.explain: Policies address user obligations, Model Specifications and Constitutions address the behavior of the model, and hard constraints are absolute lines within them.
checks.correctFeedback: All four pairs were connected correctly. The distinction between user obligations and model behavior is clear.
checks.incorrectFeedback: A few connections are out of alignment. Start by dividing documents that deal with user obligations and documents that deal with model behavior.

checks.intro: In the commentary, check the relationship between this company policy and model behavior.
checks.q: Which of the following is an appropriate explanation for the relationship between company regulations and model behavior?
options: Default behavior can be narrowed by moving regulations into system directives, but root or hard constraint level prohibitions cannot be lifted.
Hard constraints can also be resolved by writing down the person in charge in the system instructions.
Regulations cannot be reflected in model settings and are only dealt with as operational procedures.
Regulations that are difficult for the model to follow can be solved by writing long system instructions.
checks.explain: Regulations can be used to narrow down the basic behavior of a model, but high-level prohibitions cannot be lifted and the difficult parts are supplemented by operating procedures.

wrong.1: Hard constraints cannot be solved using system instructions.
wrong.2: Narrowing instructions can be transferred to system instructions.
wrong.3: Regulations that are difficult for the model to follow are not set but supplemented with procedures such as human review or logs.

checks.correctFeedback: That's correct. We identified the asymmetry that narrowing it down is possible and unraveling it is impossible.
checks.incorrectFeedback: This view misunderstands the power of instructions. Distinguish between what system instructions can and cannot do.

glossary.def: This is a document in which OpenAI discloses the model's intended behavior. Organize instructions into authority levels and include basic actions.
This is a document in which Anthropic describes Claude's values and intentions for his actions.
It is a structure that assigns authority levels to the source of instructions so that in case of conflict, the higher one wins.
This is the action the model takes when no other instructions are given. It can be adjusted within the allowable range.
A company or individual that creates products using APIs. Set up the model with system prompts.

misconceptions.myth: Model Specification is the usage policy.
misconceptions.fact: The Model Specification covers the model's behavior, and the Usage Policy covers the user's obligations. What is covered and the consequences for violations are different.

misconceptions.myth: Any restrictions on the model can be removed from the system prompt.
misconceptions.fact: Root level rules and hard constraints cannot be solved by instructions. It is the range of default behaviors that can be adjusted by system instructions.

misconceptions.myth: The model always performs the actions written in the document.
misconceptions.fact: A document is a statement of intent and goals. Differences from actual behavior must be checked separately.

closing.lead: We recapitulate the key points of this lesson.
points: The usage policy covers user obligations, and the behavioral principles document covers the behavior of the model.
The Model Spec organizes instructions into levels of authority, and the Constitution organizes instructions into priorities and subjects.
Regulations can adjust basic behavior, but they cannot lift fundamental prohibitions.
Documentation is the goal and therefore needs to be supplemented by operational procedures.
closing.reflectionLead: The following questions are for your own reflection only and will not be submitted or graded.
closing.reflection: Of the behaviors that our internal policies expect from models, which should be addressed by model settings and which should be supplemented by operating procedures?
